CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain following injury at trampoline park.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while jumping on a trampoline at a trampoline park with his wife. He heard a snap and experienced instant pain at the time of injury. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park. The pain is located on the lateral (outside) aspect of the knee. He denies regular exercise and states he was at the trampoline park for recreational purposes only. He took acetaminophen for pain relief, which provided minimal relief. He has been managing the injury by elevating the knee. He reports the ability to bear weight but notes a limp when walking. He denies trying ice or heat therapy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with knee movement and ambulation with a limp. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation on the lateral aspect of the right knee, with ecchymosis and edema noted. No effusion appreciated. Patient reports good range of motion despite pain with movement. Denies inability to bend and straighten knee.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 milligrams daily.
Metformin 500 milligrams.
Acetaminophen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does not have a consistent exercise regimen. Recently visited a trampoline park for recreation with his wife. Denies regular participation in such activities. Patient reports reluctance to seek medical care.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at 180/80 mmHg.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally.
Right knee: Tenderness to palpation on lateral aspect. Minimal tenderness on medial palpation. Ecchymosis and edema noted along lateral aspect. No effusion. Able to bend and straighten knee with pain. Gait demonstrates a limp. Able to bear weight.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain: Lateral ligament strain. Start meloxicam 15 milligrams daily for pain and swelling. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Further imaging if pain persists.
2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Order echocardiogram. Consider medication modification pending further evaluation given persistent elevation of blood pressure.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess long-term glycemic control. Order lipid panel to assess need for medication adjustment.
